In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inactivation dose of MSV is close to the D10 of Friend leukemia virus, and that 5‐FU‐sensitized MSV is significantly more UV sensitive.
Friend leukemia and MSV are sensitive to UV radiation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UV‐induced inactivation of MSV is due to damage of the viral nucleoprotein and that this damage is more pronounced when the viral RNA is modified by 5‐fluoro‐2′‐deoxyuridine.
the UV sensitivity of the murine leukemia and MSV is similar to that of the Rous sarcoma and avian myeloblastosis viruses.
the UV sensitivity of murine sarcoma and leukemia viruses is similar to the one of avian sarcoma viruses, and that the UV sensitivity is increased in the presence of 5‐fluoro‐2′‐deoxyuridine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use a single, inexpensive device to measure the UV sensitivity of viruses.
we can now use UV‐inactivated viruses to probe the mechanisms of virus entry into cells.
the use of UV inactivation can be a valuable tool for determining whether a particular virus can be considered an oncogenic virus.
